# Explainable El Niño predictability from climate mode interactions: Summary

## Research background

ENSO supplies most global seasonal climate forecast skill, yet quantifying which processes make long-lead forecasts skilful remains a long-standing challenge [abstract: ENSO skill sources challenge](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-907a2d4c36298427). Skilful prediction beyond about one year is still difficult despite decades of progress since 1986 [intro: >1-year ENSO prediction limit](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-84df85b1aaff761d). Interactions with extratropical Pacific, Indian Ocean and Atlantic modes can matter, but prior simple-model, CGCM and linear-inverse experiments have not cleanly quantified relative basin contributions amid CGCM biases and LIM limits on nonlinearity and seasonality [intro: basin interactions vs quantification gap](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-337446a5167bd34f). Contrasting 1997–1998 and 2015–2016 precursors (similar Niño3.4 amplitude, different WWV/IOD/NPMM patterns and impacts) underline why source attribution is needed [intro: 1997 vs 2015 precursors](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-fabe3a65d64eb540) [intro: distinct global impacts](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f76a70626497c7bd). AI forecasts can reach 18–24 month skill without a clear physical process link [intro: AI skill vs explainability](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-946a0ca6864a96fb).

## Core contributions

1. **Extended nonlinear recharge oscillator (XRO)**  
   XRO couples a nonlinear ENSO recharge oscillator to seasonally modulated AR(1) models for eight remote modes (NPMM, SPMM, IOB, IOD, SIOD, TNA, ATL3, SASD), enabling two-way interactions in a ten-variable state [Methods: XRO nRO+AR coupling](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-4531b156e5107e0a) [Methods: X_ENSO and X_M modes](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-9cc2cc9d73df694e). Dynamics follow equations (1)–(2) with linear operator, nonlinear terms and red-noise forcing [eq. 1: XRO state tendency](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c00af975fc62187d) [eq. 2: red-noise ξ](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-e8de420ee567f355). The linear block matrix is L = [[L_ENSO, C₁], [C₂, L_M]] (equation 3): L_ENSO is ENSO recharge–discharge, L_M is remote-mode internal dynamics, C₁ is remote feedback onto ENSO and C₂ is ENSO teleconnections to remote modes [eq. 3: L block matrix](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c82a14c19f35aff5) [Methods: L_ENSO, C₁, C₂ meanings](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-8df3e537615d1d5f). Seasonality enters via mean/annual/semi-annual expansions of L and N (equations 4–5; 515 parameters vs >100,000 in compared AI models) [Methods: seasonal fit, 515 parameters](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-db3fe7c6893dfe64).

2. **Explainable sensitivity experiment suite**  
   Relative to a Pacific-only nRO baseline (equation 6) [eq. 6: nRO](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-d6e7d7504dd32bb1), uninitialized (Uⱼ), decoupled (Dⱼ) and relaxation-to-observations (Rⱼ) designs isolate basin/mode roles; uninitialized experiments are preferred because basin contributions are nearly additive and do not overestimate remote effects [Sources: U/D/R designs](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-6d65676dd1e3fd3f) [Sources: uninitialized for additive attribution](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-aa6c31c7c00d457a) [Ext. Data Fig. 3: U additive, D overestimates](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-12de87edaf95e2e2). Skill gains from mode interactions arise mainly from remote initial-condition memory rather than ENSO-induced coupled feedbacks [Sources: memory vs coupled feedbacks](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-8ede9720eaa04c00).

3. **CMIP bias attribution and XRO2 diversity extension**  
   XROm trains L components on 91 CMIP5/6 historical runs and can replace L_ENSO, C₁ or C₂ with observational counterparts to link model biases to forecast skill [Methods: XROm L/C₁/C₂ corrections](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-89c07b82973727ab) [Results: LENSO/C₁/C₂ bias tests](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f9dc3fc8e63c2c79). XRO2 uses Niño3 and Niño4 (plus WWV) and a UCEI classifier for EP/CP/mixed types, with pantropical SSTA reconstructed from ten forecasted indices [Pantropical: XRO2 diversity](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-05536a720b76bd84) [Methods: XRO2 Niño3/Niño4](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-e5c1f3784b4103c0).

## Experimental results

1. **Simulation fidelity (ORAS5 1979–2022; 43,000-year stochastic run)**  
   XRO reproduces ENSO seasonal synchronization, Niño3.4 positive skewness, interannual spectral peak, 6–9 month WWV lead, spring persistence barrier and observed lead–lag links to other modes [Efficacy: ENSO and mode simulation](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-10a9d4b71d7b5f2c) [Methods: 45k/43k-year stochastic setup](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-cdbc96b20172c5ec).

2. **Central forecast-skill claim vs nRO, IRI/NMME and AI**  
   Out-of-sample (fit 1950–1999, verify 2002–2022): nRO matches IRI statistical-model ensemble skill; XRO beats IRI dynamical-model ensemble means at leads >9 months and reaches skill comparable to the most skilful AI model, also beating nRO for 1950–1970 and 1972–1992 verification windows [Efficacy: out-of-sample XRO vs IRI/AI](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-fe9567d9cc7f8079) [Ext. Data Fig. 2: XRO>nRO across decades](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-01a1ed67c7e1112d). Control 1979–2022 reforecasts: XRO outperforms individual dynamical models and the multi-model mean, with Niño3.4 correlation still above 0.5 at 18-month lead (again AI-comparable) [Efficacy: control skill >0.5 at 18 months](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-6a428d85cf5026fb). Cross-validation remains skilful to ~17 months; LENS perfect-model tests bound parameter-estimation correlation error to <0.1 within 21 leads [Efficacy: CV 17 months; LENS error <0.1](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-057ad022a3ea0b7a). Unlike nRO’s May–July spring predictability barrier, XRO holds ~0.5 correlation out to 16 months for all initial months [Efficacy: weakened SPB](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-1a6b71069a3ada6b).

3. **Where skill comes from (basins, modes, memory)**  
   Mode interactions raise correlation skill by up to ~0.2 (P<0.08) and weaken the SPB; ExPO/NPMM, IO/IOD and AO (TNA, SASD) contributions are strongly seasonal [Sources: +0.2 skill, SPB](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-8ede9720eaa04c00) [Sources: ExPO/IO/AO seasonality](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f1eb75d6da1f2151). IOD, NPMM and TNA dominate per-mode skill gains [Ext. Data Fig. 5: IOD/NPMM/TNA](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-bb8a80909ceaf746). Losing-memory tests show remote initial-condition memory incrementally lifts skill from nRO toward XRO [Ext. Data Fig. 4: memory extends skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-304d1afab2f61a17). Event-level examples include 1986–1987 El Niño predicted 18 vs 6 months ahead with/without remote initialization, and quantified amplitude contributions (e.g., IOD ~±0.4–0.5 °C at ~15 months; TNA ~−0.3 °C at 6–12 months) [Intensification: 18 vs 6 month event lead](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-dec017090d212958) [Intensification: IOD amplitude examples](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-a5558dee1b9265d9) [Intensification: TNA/SASD/ATL3](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-08c65582bb1177b2).

4. **Model biases, pantropical skill and ablations**  
   XROm on 91 CMIP runs is consistently less skilful than observation-trained XRO; correcting L_ENSO helps all leads and correcting C₁ helps up to ~16 months, while correcting C₂ mainly helps remote modes (e.g., IOD) more than ENSO [Biases: CMIP XROm lower skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-d098a1befc603a0f) [Ext. Data Fig. 7: bias-correction skill ranking](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-efc4caa013b149d6). Interactions extend IOB skilful lead from 5 to 19 months and IOD to 5 months (SON to 8); XRO2 captures 1997–1998 EP and 2015–2016 mixed types to 9 months where NMME fails for 1997–1998; 9-month pantropical SSTA beats operational dynamical models except over the Caribbean [Pantropical: IOB/IOD/AO skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-0cb1f91b030097af) [Pantropical: XRO2 types vs NMME](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-05536a720b76bd84) [Pantropical: 9-month map skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f188e192ec8d7860). Seasonal-cycle operators are critical for SPB suppression; ENSO nonlinearities matter for peak amplitude and El Niño→La Niña transitions, while IOD nonlinearity is negligible for ENSO skill [Methods: deseasonalizing/SPB](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-4dacc92d832f6072) [Methods: removing nonlinearity](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-ecbb44658969245c).

## Main conclusions

XRO delivers skilful, physically attributable ENSO forecasts at 16–18 month leads—better than global climate models and comparable to leading AI systems—by combining core recharge–discharge dynamics with seasonally modulated climate-mode interactions [abstract: 16–18 month explainable skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-907a2d4c36298427) [Fig. 2 caption: skilful to 16–18 months](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-25b3ee5c427c07c6). The long-range skill gain over nRO resides in remote modes’ initial-condition memory and interactions, which can be quantified as contributions to ENSO amplitude [Discussion: memory via unbiased operator](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c346a3fb7b368e83) [Sources: memory primary pathway](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-8ede9720eaa04c00). CMIP-trained reforecasts show that reducing biases in ENSO dynamics and in climate-mode interactions improves ENSO (and IOD) skill [Biases: reduced biases → skilful forecasts](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f9dc3fc8e63c2c79) [Ext. Data Fig. 8: IOD skill from bias fixes](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-681addafa485c480). Improving predictions therefore requires correct recharge-oscillator dynamics plus accurate remote-mode initial conditions, seasonally modulated memory (damping) and seasonally modulated teleconnections to ENSO; the same framework supports process-level bias diagnosis and possible extensions to higher-frequency and decadal predictability [Discussion: three compounding remote-mode requirements](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c346a3fb7b368e83) [Discussion: MJO/WWB and decadal outlook](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-e65b87702222f223).
